p.A-POLICY-WITH-NO-CHECKER-IS-A-WISH: **Scope of this document.** A policy with no checker is a wish.

p.scope-of-this-document: This file is the per-surface checklist for the attribution policy, the mechanical checks that catch slips before they publish, and the drill for when one lands anyway.

td.ROW-SURFACE-BRANCH-AND-TAG-NAMES-WHAT-LE: agent-generated branch names carrying tool names

td.ROW-SURFACE-BRANCH-AND-TAG-NAMES-CHECK: `git branch -a` eyeball at review; naming convention in the boot file

td.ROW-SURFACE-PR-TITLES-AND-DESCRIPTIONS-C: PR template with an explicit placeholder to overwrite

td.ROW-SURFACE-CI-CONFIGURATION-CHECK: review any new CI step's output once

td.ROW-SURFACE-GENERATED-FILE-HEADERS-CHECK: check scaffold output the first time a generator is adopted

pre-push.title: The pre-push scan

p.MESSAGES-AND-TRAILERS-ARE-MECHANICALLY-C: The two highest-volume surfaces — messages and trailers — are mechanically checkable.

p.pre-push-scan-lead: Run before every push (or wire as a `pre-push` hook):

pre-push.fence: # Scan outgoing commits for attribution marks. Nonzero output = stop. git log --format='%H %B' @{u}..HEAD | grep -inE 'co-authored-by|signed-off-by:.*(claude|gpt|gemini|copilot|llama|codex|model)|generated (with|by) [^ ]*(ai|llm|claude|gpt|copilot)' \ && echo 'ATTRIBUTION MARK FOUND — fix before push' || true

p.ADAPT-THE-PATTERN-LIST-TO-YOUR-OWN-TOOLS: Adapt the pattern list to the tools your team actually runs — the list above is a starting set, not an oracle.

p.a-real-hook-beats-ten-generic-ones: A hook that fires on your real tools' real phrasing is worth ten generic ones.

p.the-scan-covers-all-co-authored-by-trail: Note the scan intentionally covers *all* `Co-Authored-By` trailers: under this policy human co-authors are rare enough to allowlist by hand, and a false positive costs seconds while a false negative publishes.

p.SCANNING-CATCHES-SLIPS-CONFIGURATION-PRE: Scanning catches slips; configuration prevents them.

p.most-agents-accept-standing-instructions: Most coding agents accept standing instructions (a project rules file read at session start).

p.PUT-THE-POLICY-IN-THE-AGENTS-STANDING-IN: Put the policy there — this package's boot snippet is exactly that — and the agent stops *producing* the marks, which is cheaper than catching them.

p.SET-A-TOOLS-HARD-TRAILER-SETTING-ONCE: Where a tool has a hard setting for commit trailers, set it once and note it in the project's setup doc.

p.SLOW-SURFACES-ARE-NOT-WORTH-A-PER-PUSH-S: Slow-accumulating surfaces (comments, docs, release notes) are not worth a per-push scan.

p.periodic-audit-line-lead: Put one line in the project's periodic audit checklist (if you run `flow:health-audit` or similar):

quote.THE-AUDIT-CHECKLIST-LINE: Attribution: repo-wide grep for the pattern set; check surfaces added since last audit (new CI steps, new scaffolds, new doc generators).

facts.DRILL-CAUGHT-BEFORE-PUSH: **Caught before push:** amend or rebase locally. No further action; this is what the scan exists for.
facts.DRILL-CAUGHT-AFTER-PUSH: **Caught after push:** do **not** rewrite published history on reflex — the frozen-history rule (`flow:git-atomic-commits` §pushed) wins by default. Record the slip, fix the *source* (the tool or template that produced it), and surface to the owner: rewriting one commit's metadata out of published history is the owner's call, made knowing who has already pulled.
facts.DRILL-EITHER-WAY: **Either way:** if the same surface slips twice, the checklist — not the person — is at fault. Add the missing check.

facts.SUM-EIGHT-SURFACES-TWO-OF-THEM-MECHANICA: Eight surfaces; two of them (messages, trailers) get a mechanical pre-push scan, the rest ride templates, tool configuration, and the periodic audit.
facts.SUM-CONFIGURE-FIRST-SCAN-AS-BACKSTOP: Configure tools not to produce marks; scan as the backstop.
facts.SUM-PRE-PUSH-SLIPS-VERSUS-PUSHED-SLIPS: Pre-push slips are amended freely; pushed slips default to stand-and-fix-the-source, with history rewrite an owner-level exception.
facts.SUM-A-TWICE-SLIPPED-SURFACE-EARNS-A-LINE: A surface that slips twice earns a new checklist line.
